policy_effect: Variable-sized pools are allowed; one legal candidate is sufficient. Low, zero, or negative predicted benefit and fewer than ten replacements are not admission failures. Correctness, defined behavior, executable lowering, relocation safety, ISA/interface, memory/stack, source identity, and evidence integrity remain requirements.
scope: Named source rejections and explicit failed source/build contexts found in saved census, source-search, qualification, and diagnosis evidence. Aggregate source-suite screens stay aggregate where the preserved evidence did not record individual candidate counts.

recommendation.why: Among preserved source rejections, it has the best combination of a passed target original checksum, measured in-partition image and stack, and four already-derived relocation-safe calibrated candidates. Its only recorded admission failure was the now-removed twelve-candidate minimum. It is an integer 20x20 matrix scan, smaller and less control/pointer-heavy than the other reconsiderable leads. Two candidate formula families appear absent from the old corpus, but this is not a verified independence claim.
required_before_any_labels: reuse authenticated source/input/correctness evidence only if contract allows
verify candidate roster and exact formula families before fit
preserve all candidate outcomes including neutral/negative
do not rerun the old fixed-12 entrypoint

limitations: This is an inventory of saved evidence, not a new source-screen, replay, build, target run, or confirmation that a source remains executable under current software.
Historical reports often stop at the first gate; unknown counts and untested checks are null/explicitly unknown, not inferred passes.
Reconsidered sources are already exposed source-screen evidence and cannot be described as untouched discoveries.
A new policy does not waive correctness, defined behavior, relocation safety, ISA/lowering, stack/memory, family holdout, or measured area/timing requirements.
